title.zh: 辽宋夏金元：民族关系发展和社会变化

clips.send: Battened sails. Bamboo battens keep the sail flat. Chinese sails were stiffened by bamboo battens, so they kept their shape in strong wind. The sails could be turned to use wind from the side. They fold up quickly like a folding fan. Try the Sails slider! Battens equals the “ribs” of the sail.

clips.send: Stern rudder. Steers the ship. A large rudder hung at the stern steers the ship. A pottery boat model of the Eastern Han found in Guangzhou already has a stern rudder, one of the earliest in the world. Rudder at the back, compass on deck: steering + direction.

clips.send: Wars in the north drove another great migration south. By the Southern Song, the shift of the economic centre to the south was completed. A saying went: “When Suzhou and Huzhou have a good harvest, the whole land has enough.”

clips.send: Quanzhou harbour (Quanzhou equals chwen-joe). A world-famous port of the Song and Yuan. Quanzhou is on China’s southeast coast, about as far south as Miami. In the Song, overseas trade exceeded earlier dynasties; Guangzhou and Quanzhou were great ports known around the world. Quanzhou was a starting point of the Maritime Silk Road; merchants from Arabia, Persia and Southeast Asia came to trade. In 2021 “Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song–Yuan China” joined the UNESCO World Heritage List. Song–Yuan sea trade: remember “Guang–Quan” (Guangzhou and Quanzhou).

clips.send: Compass at sea. Northern Song: the compass goes to sea. In the Northern Song, the compass began to be used for navigation; by the Southern Song it was widely used at sea. A Northern Song book, Pingzhou Ketan, says sailors watched the stars at night, the sun by day, and the compass in cloudy weather. The compass later reached Europe through the Arabs and helped European navigators make their great voyages. Warring States: sinan spoon, Northern Song: at sea, Southern Song: widely used.

clips.send: Porcelain and silk cargo. China’s top exports. Main exports: porcelain, silk, tea and more. Song porcelain was famous across Asia and Africa. Imports: spices, ivory, pearls, medicines and other luxury goods. Song porcelain production flourished; Jingdezhen ware became famous at home and abroad. Out go porcelain and silk; in come spices and ivory.

clips.send: The Jurchen Jin (1115) destroyed the Liao (1125) and then the Northern Song (1127, the Jingkang Incident). Zhao Gou founded the Southern Song, later based in Lin’an. After peace talks the border ran along the Huai River – Dasan Pass.

clips.send: In 1206 Temüjin united the Mongol tribes and was honoured as Genghis Khan. In 1271 Kublai named his state Yuan and the next year made Dadu (today’s Beijing) the capital. In 1276 Yuan troops took Lin’an, and in 1279 the Yuan unified the whole country.

clips.send: The Yuan created the province system: the Central Secretariat ran the “heartland” around Dadu, and provinces (行省) ran the rest. The Xuanzheng Yuan governed Tibet, and the Penghu Inspectorate governed Penghu and Liuqiu (Taiwan). Today’s provinces grew out of this system.

clips.send: Song ocean-going ship. Big, strong and built for the open sea. Song shipbuilding led the world: ships were large, carried heavy loads and resisted storms. A Song ship found in Quanzhou Bay in 1974 had a hull divided into 13 compartments. What survives is about 24 m (79 ft) long, the length of a tennis court. Big ships could carry hundreds of people and sailed to Southeast Asia, South Asia, Arabia and East Africa, a sea voyage of more than 6,000 miles (10,000 km). Three “big” things about Song ships: big hull, big load, big voyages.

clips.send: Jiaozi (jyow-dzuh) paper money. The world’s earliest paper money. In the early Northern Song, “jiaozi” appeared in the Sichuan region: the earliest paper money in the world. Sichuan used heavy iron coins, which were very inconvenient for big trades (imagine paying for a bike with a wheelbarrow of quarters), so merchants began using paper notes. Jiaozi reflects the growth of trade and the commodity economy in the Song. Jiaozi: Northern Song, Sichuan, first paper money.

clips.send: Song times: the Northern Song (960) stood beside the Liao (Khitan) and the Western Xia (Tangut). In 1005 the Song and Liao made the Chanyuan Treaty: the Song paid silver and silk each year, and a long peace followed.

clips.send: Qin–Han times: the economic centre of China was the Yellow River basin in the north. The south along the Yangtze was still lightly developed.
clips.text: Qin–Han times: the economic centre of China was the Yellow River basin in the north. The south along the Yangtze was still lightly developed.

clips.send: Maritime Trade Office (Shibosi, shir-bwo-suh). The government office that managed sea trade. The Song government set up Maritime Trade Offices in Guangzhou, Quanzhou, Mingzhou and other ports to manage overseas trade. They inspected ships, collected taxes and bought goods for the state. In the Southern Song, income from sea trade became an important source of government revenue. Shi-bo equals “market + ships”: like an ancient customs house.

clips.send: After the An Lushan Rebellion in the mid-Tang, northerners again moved south in large numbers. The southern economy grew faster: the centre is moving.

clips.send: From the end of the Eastern Han through the Wei, Jin and Southern–Northern Dynasties, wars raged in the north. Many northerners moved south, and the south (Jiangnan) began to develop.

clips.send: Watertight compartments. If one compartment leaks, the ship stays afloat. Thick wooden bulkheads split the hull into separate, sealed compartments. If one compartment is holed and floods, water cannot spread to the others, so the ship can keep sailing. The bulkheads also brace the hull and make it stronger. The watertight-bulkhead technology of Chinese junks was inscribed by UNESCO in 2010 as intangible cultural heritage in need of urgent safeguarding. Try the Flooding test!

clips.send: 航海指南针。北宋时指南针开始用于航海。北宋时，指南针开始应用于航海；南宋时，指南针已广泛用于航海。。北宋朱彧的《萍洲可谈》记载：“舟师识地理，夜则观星，昼则观日，阴晦观指南针。”。指南针后来经阿拉伯人传到欧洲，为欧洲航海家的远航提供了重要条件。。战国司南，北宋用于航海，南宋广泛使用。

clips.send: 交子。世界上最早的纸币。北宋前期，四川地区出现了“交子”，这是世界上最早的纸币。。四川流通笨重的铁钱，大宗交易很不方便，于是商人开始使用纸币。。交子的出现反映了宋代商品经济的发展。。交子三要素：北宋前期、四川、最早纸币。

clips.send: 宋朝时，北宋（960年建立）与辽（契丹族）、西夏（党项族）并立。1005年宋辽订立澶渊之盟：宋每年给辽银、绢，此后双方保持了长期和平，边境贸易兴盛。

clips.send: 元朝创立行省制度：中央设中书省，直接管辖大都周围的“腹里”；地方设行中书省（简称行省）。设宣政院管辖西藏，设澎湖巡检司管辖澎湖和琉球（今台湾）。今天的“省”就是从元朝行省发展而来的。

clips.send: 泉州港。宋元时期闻名世界的大商港。宋代海外贸易超过前代，广州、泉州是闻名世界的大商港。。泉州是“海上丝绸之路”的重要起点，阿拉伯、波斯、东南亚等地商人纷纷来此贸易。。2021年，“泉州：宋元中国的世界海洋商贸中心”被列入《世界遗产名录》。。宋元海贸看“广泉”：广州、泉州。

clips.send: 水密隔舱。一舱进水，全船不沉。用厚木隔板把船体分成一个个互不相通的密封船舱。。如果一个舱破损进水，水不会流进其他舱，船仍能继续航行。。隔板还能支撑船体，让船更加坚固。。2010年，中国木帆船水密隔舱福船制造技艺被列入联合国教科文组织“急需保护的非物质文化遗产名录”。。试一试“ 进水实验”！

clips.send: 硬帆（撑条帆）。竹条撑开的风帆。中国帆船的帆用竹条撑开，大风中也能保持形状。。帆可以转动角度，能利用侧面吹来的风航行。。收帆时像折扇一样一节节叠起来，拖动“升帆”滑块试试！。撑条就是风帆的“肋骨”。

clips.send: 宋代远洋海船。船体大、结构牢、能远航。宋代造船技术居世界领先地位，海船体积大、载重多、抗风浪能力强。。1974年泉州湾出土的宋代海船，船体被分成13个船舱，残长约24米。。大海船可载数百人，远航到东南亚、南亚、阿拉伯地区和非洲东海岸。。宋船三大：船体大、载重大、航程远。
